task1.title: Time spent by UK men and women on household and leisure activities, 2008
task1.prompt: The charts below show the comparison of time spent, in minutes per day, by UK's males and females on household and leisure activities in 2008.

chartDesc.overview: Overall, men spent more time on most leisure activities than women, especially TV, video, and radio, whereas women spent significantly more time on household chores like cooking, washing, and ironing. Repair was the only household task where men spent more time than women.
keyFeatures: From the table: TV, video, and radio accounted for the highest leisure time for both genders, with men averaging 137 minutes per day compared to 118 minutes for women.
From the table: Time spent reading was nearly identical between men (18 minutes) and women (19 minutes).
From the bar chart: Cooking and washing was the most time-consuming household task for women at 75 minutes per day, almost three times higher than men (27 minutes).

From the bar chart: Men spent more time than women on repair activities (20 minutes vs 7 minutes), whereas women spent over double the time men spent on clothes washing and ironing (30 minutes vs 12 minutes).

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
